# [[Review] Family Adventure at Bangkok Safari & Marine Park]

By Money Saving Daddy

13 Jan 2024

* * *

[WhatsApp][Facebook][Telegram][Share]

Our [adventure]to the [Bangkok Safari & Marine Park] was driven by the desire to find a balance between fun and education for our children.

Situated on the outskirts of Bangkok, this destination promised a day filled with unique animal encounters and learning opportunities.

## **Location:**

The park's convenient location outside Bangkok made it an ideal getaway. We chose a transport service that included ticket purchases, but I later realized that booking tickets online could have saved us money, a tip worth sharing for future visitors.

You may want to also plan Chocolate Ville for the same day itinerary as it is just 20-30 mins away from the Safari Zoo.

## **Preparation:**

Preparation involved packing essentials like sunscreen, hats, and comfortable walking shoes for a day of exploration.

Booking tickets [online]can offer discounts and is a good way to save some money.

## **Detailed Day Itinerary :**

![Image 2: 7 Days Bangkok travel with Kids 14]

![Image 3: 7 Days Bangkok travel with Kids 13]

![Image 4: 7 Days Bangkok travel with Kids 07]

![Image 5: 7 Days Bangkok travel with Kids 19]

![Image 6: 7 Days Bangkok travel with Kids 17]

* **10:00 AM - Orangutan Show:** Our day began with the playful and engaging Orangutan Show. This was a fantastic start, as it was included in the entrance fee and offered both entertainment and a glimpse into the intelligence of these creatures.
* **11:00 AM - Elephant Show:** Next, we were captivated by the majestic elephants. This show was not only entertaining but also an eye opener for the kids that these huge animals can perform certain tricks.
* **12:00 PM - Lunch:** For lunch, our driver drove us out for lunch.
* **1:00 PM - Safari Drive-In:** The drive-in safari allowed us to see various animals in more naturalistic settings, which was both exciting and educational for the kids. It is pretty up close and personal. If you waited till 2.30pm, you may get to see the tiger feeding in the safari itself.
* **2:00 PM - Giraffe Feeding Encounter:** For 150 baht per bucket, the giraffe feeding was an affordable and unforgettable experience. It was interactive and fun, allowing us to get up close with these gentle giants.
* **3:30 PM - Tiger Photo Encounter:** The tiger photo encounter, costing 500 baht per person, was a thrilling and unique experience. It provided an up-close look at these beautiful animals, making for a memorable photo opportunity. Although it is just less than 1 minute.
* **3.45 PM - Orangutan Photo Encounter:** Similarly, the orangutan photo encounter, also 500 baht per person, was a delightful experience. Getting close to these fascinating primates was a highlight for the kids.

## **Pros and Cons:**

### **Good:**

* **Variety of Activities:** The park offered a wide range of shows and encounters, ensuring there was something interesting for everyone.
* **Educational Aspect:** Each show and encounter was designed to be informative, teaching us about different animal species and conservation efforts.
* **Interactive Nature:** The interactive experiences like feeding giraffes and the photo encounters were particularly memorable, allowing personal interaction with the animals.

### **Not so good:**

* **Limited Food Options:** The limited and slightly expensive food options within the park could be a concern, especially for families with children. Hence, our driver also took us out for lunch at a local eatery. Food are pretty affordable there.
* **Extra Costs:** While the entry fee was reasonable, the additional expenses for special encounters like the photos was abit turn off. But then again, if it is include in the ticket, we would see long queues for the photo encounters.

## **Costing:**

![Image 7: Bangkok Safari Zoo Ticket]

* **Entry Fees:** The entrance fee to the park was in line with the variety of experiences it offered. 1200baht for adults, 1100 baht for kids. Online tickets are cheaper if they have promotion [[Check here for details]]
* **Special Encounters:** Additional charges were applicable for unique experiences like the giraffe feeding (150 baht per bucket) and photo encounters (500 baht per person for both tigers and orangutans).
* **Transport:**3000 baht, include pick up and hotel till drop off at Chocolate Ville.

Our day at the Bangkok Safari & Marine Park was a remarkable mix of adventure, learning, and fun. It's an excellent destination for families visiting Bangkok.

To make the most of your visit, consider booking tickets online, preparing a budget for additional experiences, and possibly bringing your own snacks.

# Safari World Bangkok: Thailand’s Greatest Open Zoo and Marine Park

**TL;DR:** Safari World Bangkok is Thailand’s top open zoo and marine park, featuring safari drives with lions and giraffes, dolphin shows, orangutan boxing, and family rides. Located on the outskirts of Bangkok, open daily 9am-5pm; with tickets around 400-1500 THB. It’s usually close to a full day of family fun, so can be bundled into a single day or multi day tour with Your Thai Guide. For transport, tickets, and guided insights, [contact us] to build Safari World into your own custom private tour!

## Why Visit Safari World Bangkok

At _Your Thai Guide_, we arrange family friendly tours that make Bangkok’s world class attractions like Safari World unforgettable. This is Thailand’s greatest open zoo, blending thrilling wildlife safaris, marine shows, and theme park fun. From driving through savannahs with hundreds of animals to interactive shows, it’s a rare experience you won’t find many other places. Ideal for kids and adults, Safari World offers something for everyone in the family.

![Image 4: Safari drive at Safari World Bangkok open zoo with lions and giraffes]

## Highlights of Safari World Bangkok

Safari World is divided into Safari Park and Marine Park, with attractions that highlight animal intelligence, power, and fun.

### Safari Park: Open Zoo Adventure

Take a 45 minute, 8 kilometer drive (or guided tram) through natural habitats, an amzing addition to a family day out in Bangkok.

* **Animals on Display**: See lions, tigers, zebras, giraffes, ostriches, and Himalayan black bears in open savannah settings.
* **Feeding Shows**: Watch powerful tigers and lions during live feeding, showcasing conservation and animal behaviors.
* **Tip**: Go early for active animals.

### Marine Park: Shows and Rides

This section combines zoo exhibits with theme park excitement, featuring must see marine park shows in Bangkok.

* **Sea Lion Show**: Funny sea lions perform tricks at Lighthouse Cove, engaging and colorful for the kids.
* **Jungle Cruise**: Exciting log flume ride through crocodile filled waters with gorillas and head hunters.
* **Hollywood Cowboy Stunt Show**: High energy stunts, explosions, and chases. Pure adrenaline!
* **Dolphin Show**: Intelligent dolphins flip and interact, get a handshake or kiss.
* **Bird Show**: Parrots and macaws perform choreographed tricks and talking acts.
* **Jungle Walk/Safari Terrace**: Feed giraffes bananas for photos and licks, a highlight not to miss.
* **Orangutan Boxing**: NOTE – Intented to be light hearted fun, this is considered controversal by many, so discretion is advised.
* **Eggs World**: Educational exhibit on animal eggs, a great learning break.
* **Spy War**: High-octane spy show with explosions and action.

![Image 6: Dolphin show at Safari World Bangkok marine park for family day out]

## Dining and Amenities

Stay fueled for a full day: Jungle Cruise and Safari restaurants offer buffets, with fast-food outlets and carts for snacks like grilled items. Shop souvenirs at the gift store. Everything is self contained, so no need to leave the park.

![Image 8: Giraffe feeding platform at Safari World Bangkok open zoo]

## Practical Tips for Your Safari World Visit

Safari World is 40km from central Bangkok, so taxis or private transport are most practical, especially with kids. Plan a full day (9am-5pm) to explore. _Your Thai Guide_ can bundle it into a single or multi-day custom tour with transport from your hotel.

* **Opening Hours**: Daily 9am-5pm.
* **Safari World Tickets**: During peak season, ask us to help book beforehand. Some small children may be free. Adults 400-1500 Baht, Children 300-1400 Baht (single or combo for both safari and water park).
* **Best Time**: Early mornings for active animals and best show seats.
* **Family Tips**: Wear comfy shoes, bring sunscreen/water. Stroller-friendly with shaded areas.

If you do spend less than a full day at the Safari park and want to add in one other stop close by:

1. Fashion Island Mall is 10-12 mins away. Easy, Air-Conditioned, Low Effort  
 2. The Promenade is in same area as Fashion Island. Relaxed Mall + Architecture  
 3. Kwan Riam Floating Market is 10-12 mins away, open Sat-Sun  
 4. Wat Bang Peng Tai is 20 mins away, photogenic riverside temple

### Our animal encounters in Safari World Bangkok

 Posted by ~Summer~ on July 04, 2018 
in [Around the world in 80 days], [Giveaways Reviews Advertorials]

Whenever we go on a holiday, we always try to make it a point to visit the zoo. This is because the kids, who take after us, love animals and every visit is bound to be a learning experience filled with fun and laughter. So far, we have set foot in zoos and safaris in Singapore, Bali, Taiwan, Prague, Zurich, Vienna, Stockholm and more. Thus, it was only natural that our Bangkok trip (read about our full itinerary [here]) included a visit to the popular **[Safari World]**.  
  
 In this post, we share with you all the sights we saw and fun experiences we had in Safari World. For those of you who are planning for a family trip to Bangkok soon and would love to visit the park too, don't forget to book your attraction tickets via [Klook] to enjoy discounts!

[![Image 2]]

  
 Safari World started in the year 1988 and has developed into a popular tourist destination that now consists of two parks - Safari Park and Marine Park. It is open all year round from 9:00am to 5:00pm so it would be good to plan your visit such that you can arrive early and have the whole day to explore both parks. For us, we came here straightaway after our flight landed and we arrived at about 10:30am after over an hour's drive. Yes, it might sound exhausting but we really wanted to make full use of every day we had on this 5D4N trip.  
  
[![Image 3]]  
 Even though Safari World's [website] is not a very comprehensive one and only provides the basic information, it won't be hard to navigate your way around the park because of the maps provided (you can also find it in the brochure given at the entrance). Guide maps like the one below, which you can see in the parks, indicate clearly the locations of the various animal exhibits, the show venues, restaurants, toilets and other facilities available.  
  

[![Image 4]]

  
 There are also directional signboards that are written in Thai, English and Chinese to help visitors to find their way around easily. 
  
[![Image 5]]  
  

 The animal shows are one of the highlights at Safari World so if you can, do try to include at least a couple of them during your visit. We wanted to watch the Elephant show but alas the show venue was too far from where we were at that time (11:40am) and though we were right outside the Cowboy Stunt show, the boy heard the loud noises which included gunshots and cowboys yelling yeehaw so he got scared and didn't want us to enter. However, we did manage to catch the Dolphin show which was pretty awesome and impressive, which I'll share more of below.

  

[![Image 6]]

  
  

[![Image 7]]

 First, I want to tell you more about the unique highlight at Safari World and that is... there is a drive through where you can come up close with the animals! You can either rent a car and drive in yourself, arrange for a private car transfer, take a taxi and ride in, or go on the coach tours offered at Safari World too.

  

[![Image 8]]

  
  

[![Image 9]]

  

[![Image 10]]

  
 For us, we were very blessed that our local friend was able to meet us that day so he took us for a ride in his car. Since we wanted to take things at a leisurely pace, we took our time to stop and admire each and every animal species, even winding down our windows so we could have an clear, unobstructed view and even be able to say "Hello" to all the friendly animals. This was probably something we couldn't have done if we were riding in the coach. Phew!  
  
[![Image 11]]  
  

[![Image 12]]

  

[![Image 13]]

  
 I can't tell you how ecstatic the kids were to see the animals and they just kept talking all at once and scrambling to see the animals on either side of the window. Every time they spotted an animal - it doesn't matter what animal - they would squeal in joy and ask everyone to come and see too! Thankfully, no one seemed whiny or tired after the flight and we were off to a great start for our expedition.  

  

[![Image 14]]

  

[![Image 15]]

  
[![Image 16]]  
  
  
 Now, our hearts started to beat a little faster when we entered a tall gate which was fenced up at both sides and saw the words "Do not wind down your windows". Guess who we were going to meet?  
  
[![Image 17]]  
  

[![Image 18]]

  

[![Image 19]]

  
 Yup, the lions! Alas most of them were sleeping and though I was hoping that they were just tired after the feeding show in the morning, it would be hard to deny that they seemed a little drugged and all they wanted to do was lie down and rest. We did hear that Safari World got into some controversy a few years back over its treatment of animals but I sincerely hoped they had learnt a lesson and started treating the animals the way they deserve to be treated.  
  
 On the other hand, the tigers seemed much more alert and would look at us when we drove past. A couple of them were also walking around or swimming in the waters and it was definitely a first for us to get so up close to these supposedly ferocious, man-eating creatures.  
  

[![Image 20]]

  
 The whole drive through took us about 40 minutes and subsequently, we explored the rest of the park on foot. For those of you with young kids, you can consider renting these dolphin strollers which are cute to the max and very affordable too!  
  

[![Image 21]]

  

[![Image 22]]

  
 Our first stop was to find lunch since it was almost noon and it took us a while because there were just so many distractions along the way. From animal statues which make great photo opportunities....  
  

[![Image 23]]

  
 and a colourful train that kids can climb on board...  
  

[![Image 24]]

  
 to a river filled with colourful boats and graceful swans...  
  

[![Image 25]]

  
 and roaming animal mascots too!  
  
 Note that these mascots kind of expect that you give them a tip after you take a photo. It doesn't have to be a lot and a little will go a long way to make their day.  
  

[![Image 26]]

  
 We checked out one of the restaurants and saw that they were serving a normal lunch buffet. However, the prices were considerably exorbitant and a lunch would cost our family of five over a thousand baht. So we decided to give it a miss and see what else we could find. And thankfully we did so because we soon came across these 'Fast Food' stalls near the river which were selling local delights at much affordable prices.  
  

[![Image 27]]

  
 For instance, we ordered this Pork Leg Rice for just 80 baht, which is just slightly over SGD3. Cheap, right? It was also quite tasty and very filling too!  
  

[![Image 28]]

  

[![Image 29]]

  

[![Image 30]]

  
 Our favourite was the Rungsit Boat noodles (beef/pork) which had such an authentic Thai flavour to it and even the kids loved it so much that we ordered a second helping. It was fascinating to see how the Thai ladies would cook the noodles on their boats, pick out the raw vegetables and serve you a bowl of piping hot soup noodles. You can choose if you prefer bee hoon or kway teow and if your kids are like us and love fishballs, you can also ask for a bowl of fishballs soup too. Yummy!  
  

[![Image 31]]

  
[![Image 32]]  
 We also ordered a plate of Phad Thai and drinks and to total up, the whole lunch cost us less than 400 baht which is pretty amazing considering that we were at a tourist attraction. Yup, you can never find food at such prices in Singapore attractions.  
  

[![Image 33]]

  
 After lunch, we continued with our exploration enthusiastically and more energetically, woohoo! There was this Adventure Island where you can play in carnival games and win prizes too. ![Image 3: safari-world-ราคาบัตร](blob:http://localhost/74c0f92e37e9ab12c0455c942567915d)
ซาฟารีเวิลด์ Safari World 2026 ไฉไล กว่าเดิมมีโซนใหม่ให้เด็กๆ และครอบครัวไปเที่ยวกันฉ่ำๆ ไปเที่ยวซาฟารีเวิลด์ อาณาจักรของเหล่าสัตว์น้อยใหญ่เต็มไปด้วยความน่ารัก ซาฟารีเวิลด์ เป็นสวนสัตว์ใหญ่ที่สุดในกรุงเทพฯ โดยแบ่งพื้นที่ให้เลือกเที่ยวชมความน่ารักของสัตว์น้อยสัตว์ใหญ่ไว้ 2 โซน คือ _โซน Marine Park_ เดินเที่ยวชมสัตว์ได้อย่างอิสระ ชมโชว์เจ๋งๆ จากสัตว์น่ารักแสนฉลาด และ _โซน Safari Park_ ซาฟารีเวิลด์ สวนสัตว์เปิด สามารถขับรถเที่ยวเองได้แบบใกล้ชิดกับบรรดาสัตว์กว่า 100 ชีวิต ซาฟารีเวิลด์ ราคาบัตรทั้ง 2 โซน เริ่มต้น ผู้ใหญ่ 750 บาท เด็ก 650 บาท

## ****โซน Marine Park มารีนปาร์คคือ****

ซาฟารีเวิลด์ โซนมารีนปาร์ค จะเน้นโชว์การแสดงของสัตว์ต่างๆ เป็นรอบๆ เช่น โชว์โลมา โชว์สิงโตทะเล หรือกิจกรรมสนุกๆ อย่าง ให้อาหารนกแก้วซันคอนัวร์ ให้อาหารจิงโจ้ ให้อาหารยีราฟ ให้อาหารอูฐ อีกทั้งยังมีร้านอาหาร คาเฟ่ ขายของที่ระลึกมากมาย

### **โซน Lory World และ Lory’s Coffee & Eatery**

Lory World โซนใหม่น้องนกจิ๋วแต่เสียงแจ๋ว พร้อมมุมชิลๆ กินอาหารและคาเฟ่กับเครื่องดื่ม นั่งถ่ายรูปชิคๆ คูลได้ๆ เลย ไฮไลต์โซนนี้คือ นกโนรี สีสันสดใส เรียกได้ว่าเป็นอาณาจักรเลยก็ได้ เพราะมีเจ้านกโนรีสดใสระรานตา เพื่อความสนุกและเอ็นจอย แนะนำให้ซื้อนมป้อนน้องนก ได้รูปสวยจัดเลย น้องนกจะมาคลอเคลียปะหนึ่งเพื่อนสนิทคิดไม่สื่อเพราะจิกหัว เอ้ยกินอาหารอย่างเอร็ดอร่อย ไม่มีอาหารนกไม่มาหานะ นำให้ยื่นมือไปยาวๆ เพราะนกเขาก็กลัวเราเหมือนกันมือนิ่งๆ เดี๋ยวเขาก็มาหาเราเอง ให้อาหารน้องอิ่มแล้วก็อย่าลืมเติมท้องว่างๆ ให้กับตัวเองกันต่อ ที่โซน Lory’s Coffee & Eatery ใกล้ๆ กัน มีพิซซ่าอบร้อนๆ ครัวซ็อง และ เครื่องดื่มกาแฟด้วยนะ พิกัดใกล้ๆ Camp Kangaroo และ Parrot Lane

### **Tree House Aviary & Kitchen**

หลังจากปิดบริการไปสักพักใหญ่ ซาฟารีเวิร์ล ก็ไม่ปล่อยให้พื้นที่เหงาๆ ได้มีการการปรับภูมิทัศน์ให้มีความสวยงามมากกว่าเดิม พร้อมเพิ่มโซนและกิจกรรมใหม่เพียบเลย เริ่มต้นด้วย “Tree House Aviary & Kitchen” โฉมใหม่ของ Mini World โลกของนก Sun Conure (ซันคอนัวร์) น่ารักมากสดใสไปทั้งโซนเต็มไปด้วยนกซันคอนัวร์ 200 ตัว เปิดประสบการณ์ความสนุกแบบ Edutainment นอกจากได้เข้าไปสัมผัสนกเล็กสีสันสดใสอย่างใกล้ชิดแล้ว ยังสร้างความสนุกผ่านการเรียนรู้ให้กับเด็กๆ ด้วยการให้อาหารนกแนวใหม่ ผ่าน ‘โคนไอศกรีม’ อาหารนก ผลิตเองด้วยสูตรผ่านการวิจัยโดยทีมผู้เชี่ยวชาญด้านนก และสัตวแพทย์ของซาฟารีเวิลด์ บอกเลยว่าถือเป็นโลกแห่งการเรียนรู้แบบใหม่ ไม่มีที่อื่นใดในโลก ด้วยค่าเข้าชมเริ่มต้นเพียง 50 บาท/ท่าน และโคนไอศกรีมอาหารนก เริ่มต้น 100 บาท ปล. อย่าเผลอแอบกินขนมน้องนกนะ เพราะสีสันน่ากินมาก

### Our animal encounters in Safari World Bangkok

 Posted by ~Summer~ on July 04, 2018 
in [Around the world in 80 days], [Giveaways Reviews Advertorials]

Whenever we go on a holiday, we always try to make it a point to visit the zoo. This is because the kids, who take after us, love animals and every visit is bound to be a learning experience filled with fun and laughter. So far, we have set foot in zoos and safaris in Singapore, Bali, Taiwan, Prague, Zurich, Vienna, Stockholm and more. Thus, it was only natural that our Bangkok trip (read about our full itinerary [here]) included a visit to the popular **[Safari World]**.  
  
 In this post, we share with you all the sights we saw and fun experiences we had in Safari World. For those of you who are planning for a family trip to Bangkok soon and would love to visit the park too, don't forget to book your attraction tickets via [Klook] to enjoy discounts!

[![Image 2]]

  
 Safari World started in the year 1988 and has developed into a popular tourist destination that now consists of two parks - Safari Park and Marine Park. It is open all year round from 9:00am to 5:00pm so it would be good to plan your visit such that you can arrive early and have the whole day to explore both parks. For us, we came here straightaway after our flight landed and we arrived at about 10:30am after over an hour's drive. Yes, it might sound exhausting but we really wanted to make full use of every day we had on this 5D4N trip.  
  
[![Image 3]]  
 Even though Safari World's [website] is not a very comprehensive one and only provides the basic information, it won't be hard to navigate your way around the park because of the maps provided (you can also find it in the brochure given at the entrance). Guide maps like the one below, which you can see in the parks, indicate clearly the locations of the various animal exhibits, the show venues, restaurants, toilets and other facilities available.  
  

[![Image 4]]

  
 There are also directional signboards that are written in Thai, English and Chinese to help visitors to find their way around easily. 
  
[![Image 5]]  
  

 The animal shows are one of the highlights at Safari World so if you can, do try to include at least a couple of them during your visit. We wanted to watch the Elephant show but alas the show venue was too far from where we were at that time (11:40am) and though we were right outside the Cowboy Stunt show, the boy heard the loud noises which included gunshots and cowboys yelling yeehaw so he got scared and didn't want us to enter. However, we did manage to catch the Dolphin show which was pretty awesome and impressive, which I'll share more of below.

  

[![Image 6]]

  
  

[![Image 7]]

 First, I want to tell you more about the unique highlight at Safari World and that is... there is a drive through where you can come up close with the animals! You can either rent a car and drive in yourself, arrange for a private car transfer, take a taxi and ride in, or go on the coach tours offered at Safari World too.

  

[![Image 8]]

  
  

[![Image 9]]

  

[![Image 10]]

  
 For us, we were very blessed that our local friend was able to meet us that day so he took us for a ride in his car. Since we wanted to take things at a leisurely pace, we took our time to stop and admire each and every animal species, even winding down our windows so we could have an clear, unobstructed view and even be able to say "Hello" to all the friendly animals. This was probably something we couldn't have done if we were riding in the coach. Phew!  
  
[![Image 11]]  
  

[![Image 12]]

  

[![Image 13]]

  
 I can't tell you how ecstatic the kids were to see the animals and they just kept talking all at once and scrambling to see the animals on either side of the window. Every time they spotted an animal - it doesn't matter what animal - they would squeal in joy and ask everyone to come and see too! Thankfully, no one seemed whiny or tired after the flight and we were off to a great start for our expedition.  

  

[![Image 14]]

  

[![Image 15]]

  
[![Image 16]]  
  
  
 Now, our hearts started to beat a little faster when we entered a tall gate which was fenced up at both sides and saw the words "Do not wind down your windows". Guess who we were going to meet?  
  
[![Image 17]]  
  

[![Image 18]]

  

[![Image 19]]

  
 Yup, the lions! Alas most of them were sleeping and though I was hoping that they were just tired after the feeding show in the morning, it would be hard to deny that they seemed a little drugged and all they wanted to do was lie down and rest. We did hear that Safari World got into some controversy a few years back over its treatment of animals but I sincerely hoped they had learnt a lesson and started treating the animals the way they deserve to be treated.  
  
 On the other hand, the tigers seemed much more alert and would look at us when we drove past. A couple of them were also walking around or swimming in the waters and it was definitely a first for us to get so up close to these supposedly ferocious, man-eating creatures.  
  

[![Image 20]]

  
 The whole drive through took us about 40 minutes and subsequently, we explored the rest of the park on foot. For those of you with young kids, you can consider renting these dolphin strollers which are cute to the max and very affordable too!  
  

[![Image 21]]

  

[![Image 22]]

  
 Our first stop was to find lunch since it was almost noon and it took us a while because there were just so many distractions along the way. From animal statues which make great photo opportunities....  
  

[![Image 23]]

  
 and a colourful train that kids can climb on board...  
  

[![Image 24]]

  
 to a river filled with colourful boats and graceful swans...  
  

[![Image 25]]

  
 and roaming animal mascots too!  
  
 Note that these mascots kind of expect that you give them a tip after you take a photo. It doesn't have to be a lot and a little will go a long way to make their day.  
  

[![Image 26]]

  
 We checked out one of the restaurants and saw that they were serving a normal lunch buffet. However, the prices were considerably exorbitant and a lunch would cost our family of five over a thousand baht. So we decided to give it a miss and see what else we could find. And thankfully we did so because we soon came across these 'Fast Food' stalls near the river which were selling local delights at much affordable prices.  
  

[![Image 27]]

  
 For instance, we ordered this Pork Leg Rice for just 80 baht, which is just slightly over SGD3. Cheap, right? It was also quite tasty and very filling too!  
  

[![Image 28]]

  

[![Image 29]]

  

[![Image 30]]

  
 Our favourite was the Rungsit Boat noodles (beef/pork) which had such an authentic Thai flavour to it and even the kids loved it so much that we ordered a second helping. It was fascinating to see how the Thai ladies would cook the noodles on their boats, pick out the raw vegetables and serve you a bowl of piping hot soup noodles. You can choose if you prefer bee hoon or kway teow and if your kids are like us and love fishballs, you can also ask for a bowl of fishballs soup too. Yummy!  
  

[![Image 31]]

  
[![Image 32]]  
 We also ordered a plate of Phad Thai and drinks and to total up, the whole lunch cost us less than 400 baht which is pretty amazing considering that we were at a tourist attraction. Yup, you can never find food at such prices in Singapore attractions.  
  

[![Image 33]]

  
 After lunch, we continued with our exploration enthusiastically and more energetically, woohoo! There was this Adventure Island where you can play in carnival games and win prizes too. Note: Prizes means stuffed toys and more stuffed toys. The good thing is the games are not expensive so if you have time to spare, you can let the kids have some fun here.  
  

[![Image 34]]

  

[![Image 35]]

  
 Right outside Adventure Island, we saw a crowd forming and went to take a look at the commotion. Well, they were doing the touristy thing by letting park visitors take photos with real live orangutans and tiger cubs, which they will put it in a nice frame and let you bring home.  
  
 Very touristy, right?  
  
 Well, and so....  
  
 We did that touristy thing. All because the kids said they would like to take a photo with a tiger, which seemed totally cool and horrifying at the same time. Even the two-year-old said he wanted to join in too and the hubby suggested that we just let the kids do it, which made it sound even more horrifying to me. Haha.  
  
 Unlike what we see in some other zoos, these tiger cubs looked very sober, not groggy, and they were also able to focus on drinking their milk from the milk bottles. Yup, sounds cute, right? Wait till you see the size of the supposedly 'baby' tiger that my kids carried.  
  

[![Image 36]]

  
 Yup, it was big and long enough to lay across all of their laps. The big girl was tasked to take the bottle and feed the cub (you can see that its eyes are open!), the little sister was to hold its body, and the toddler was asked to just sit in the middle and smile. Haha. The big girl got scratched a little at the end of it because the cub's nails were so long! But if you were to ask her if she would do it again, she would definitely say yes. I mean, how many times does this kind of opportunity come across in your life?  
  
 Anyway, for those of you who wanna know, it costs 700 baht to do this but they do give you quite a pretty Safari World photo frame (made of cardboard, okay? Don't expect too much) along with your photo.

### **โซน Lory World และ Lory’s Coffee & Eatery**

Lory World โซนใหม่น้องนกจิ๋วแต่เสียงแจ๋ว พร้อมมุมชิลๆ กินอาหารและคาเฟ่กับเครื่องดื่ม นั่งถ่ายรูปชิคๆ คูลได้ๆ เลย ไฮไลต์โซนนี้คือ นกโนรี สีสันสดใส เรียกได้ว่าเป็นอาณาจักรเลยก็ได้ เพราะมีเจ้านกโนรีสดใสระรานตา เพื่อความสนุกและเอ็นจอย แนะนำให้ซื้อนมป้อนน้องนก ได้รูปสวยจัดเลย น้องนกจะมาคลอเคลียปะหนึ่งเพื่อนสนิทคิดไม่สื่อเพราะจิกหัว เอ้ยกินอาหารอย่างเอร็ดอร่อย ไม่มีอาหารนกไม่มาหานะ นำให้ยื่นมือไปยาวๆ เพราะนกเขาก็กลัวเราเหมือนกันมือนิ่งๆ เดี๋ยวเขาก็มาหาเราเอง ให้อาหารน้องอิ่มแล้วก็อย่าลืมเติมท้องว่างๆ ให้กับตัวเองกันต่อ ที่โซน Lory’s Coffee & Eatery ใกล้ๆ กัน มีพิซซ่าอบร้อนๆ ครัวซ็อง และ เครื่องดื่มกาแฟด้วยนะ พิกัดใกล้ๆ Camp Kangaroo และ Parrot Lane

### **Tree House Aviary & Kitchen**

หลังจากปิดบริการไปสักพักใหญ่ ซาฟารีเวิร์ล ก็ไม่ปล่อยให้พื้นที่เหงาๆ ได้มีการการปรับภูมิทัศน์ให้มีความสวยงามมากกว่าเดิม พร้อมเพิ่มโซนและกิจกรรมใหม่เพียบเลย เริ่มต้นด้วย “Tree House Aviary & Kitchen” โฉมใหม่ของ Mini World โลกของนก Sun Conure (ซันคอนัวร์) น่ารักมากสดใสไปทั้งโซนเต็มไปด้วยนกซันคอนัวร์ 200 ตัว เปิดประสบการณ์ความสนุกแบบ Edutainment นอกจากได้เข้าไปสัมผัสนกเล็กสีสันสดใสอย่างใกล้ชิดแล้ว ยังสร้างความสนุกผ่านการเรียนรู้ให้กับเด็กๆ ด้วยการให้อาหารนกแนวใหม่ ผ่าน ‘โคนไอศกรีม’ อาหารนก ผลิตเองด้วยสูตรผ่านการวิจัยโดยทีมผู้เชี่ยวชาญด้านนก และสัตวแพทย์ของซาฟารีเวิลด์ บอกเลยว่าถือเป็นโลกแห่งการเรียนรู้แบบใหม่ ไม่มีที่อื่นใดในโลก ด้วยค่าเข้าชมเริ่มต้นเพียง 50 บาท/ท่าน และโคนไอศกรีมอาหารนก เริ่มต้น 100 บาท ปล. อย่าเผลอแอบกินขนมน้องนกนะ เพราะสีสันน่ากินมาก
